title: Chamier: the general prayer of saints is likely but not proven
source_text: XLVI. Similiter Chamierus quaestione proposita, utrum Sanctorum animae pro nobis orent in genere; hoc est universaliter pro Ecclesia Christiana, & fidelium universitate, pronunciat id nullo certo argumento constare: quamvis fateatur nonnihil habere veri similitudinis; & rem relinquat in medio, ut quisque fruatur suo judicio. Panstr. tom. 2. lib. 8. cap. 5.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly Chamier, the question being proposed, whether the souls of the Saints pray for us in general; that is universally for the Christian Church, and the whole body of the faithful, pronounces that this is established by no certain argument: although he admits that it has something of likelihood; and he leaves the matter in the middle, so that each may enjoy his own judgment. Panstratia, volume 2, book 8, chapter 5.
pass_b_english: Chamier likewise takes up the question whether the souls of the saints pray for us in general, that is, for the Christian Church as a whole and for the whole body of believers. He declares that no certain argument establishes it, though he grants it has some likelihood, and he leaves the matter open for each to decide for himself. (Panstratia, volume 2, book 8, chapter 5.)

lemmas.gloss: leaves the matter in the middle

choices.why: An idiom for undecided questions; 'open' conveys it without a literal 'in the middle'.
